chromosome names seem to be different. If they are different unite() won't work. They have to have the same naming convention.

You can make a reproducible example with subset of the data, that's the main point. Here are some ideas:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5963269/how-to-make-a-great-r-reproducible-example

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Is it possible to use methylkit for calculating the average methylation rate for a genomic region (promoter for example) annotated with gene name or ID for each gene.

The desired output :
gene_name   promoter_methylation rate
NM_199260   0.08
NM_199277   0.72
NM_199333   0.123

Thank you in advance ..

messages.body_plain:
Hello

I am trying to analyze human WGBS data using Bismark and methylkit package. I found some discrepancy in %methylation and trying to understand the results.

In Bismark report ~75% methylation is seen in CpG context as shown in below graph https://ibb.co/85SJ7TF

But when I look at % CpG methylation per base using getMethylationStats(), I see very low methylation levels as seen in below graph. https://ibb.co/8xYrFgZ

Can someone help me understand why I see such discrepancy and how to interpret the results? If there are high levels of methylated Cs, shouldn't we expect more methylation at CpG base. Am I interpreting the graph the right way? Is it an issue with methylKit because the total number of nucleotides calculated is not close to the same. Total C's analyzed in Bismark is 1e+e10, whereas the highest number is on the 6e+08 scale for methylkit.

Thanks, Pooja

Many thanks,

Ian

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I keep IDs of loci when performing PCASamples?
messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] How can I keep IDs of loci when performing PCASamples?
messages.body_plain:
I worked it out! Starting with a methylBaseDB object called 'meth_red'...

obj <- percMethylation(meth_red, rowids=TRUE)

rv <- apply(obj, MARGIN = 1, FUN = var) # MARGIN=1 means apply the function to rows # 'MARGIN=1' means apply the function to rows, 'FUN = var' means calculate variance

obj2 <- obj[rv > quantile(rv, probs = 0.5), ] #Creates a new methylBaseDB object containing only those rows that have a variance in the top 50% values
pca <- prcomp(t(obj2), center=TRUE, scale.=TRUE)

'pca' now contains the exact same loading scores as a PCASamples default run would, but with the added bonus of listing the loci which those loadings describe.

Thanks for the advice, Altuna, and I hope this is useful to others :)

Ian
